clock: the computer that ran the builder (UK time on Richard's PC)

rule.bands: A above 90%; B+ above 82.5% to 90%; B above 75% to 82.5%; C+ above 66.67% to 75%; C above 58.33% to 66.67%; C- above 50% to 58.33%; D above 25% to 50%; F up to 25%
rule.rank: percentile rank = (scores below + half the ties) / population size; the population of an item is every stock holding a score on that item from its registered run (or its published memo)
rule.registered_run: the newest live card in the conveyor's trays whose run holds scores; dry, cancelled and control runs never enter
rule.boundaries: per item, the lowest score that earned each grade today; null where no score earned that grade
rule.comparison_set: the stocks analysed by the new approach (the Sets of Questions/Items approach)
rule.fixed_letters: on memo topics 5, 6, 8, 11 and 12 a cell carrying fixed_letter shows the Rater's own letter from a real-world measure (A to F, no sub-grade), never re-cut; its rank and p are information only (D-SQ-267, D-SQ-271)
rule.fixed_cutoffs: v1.5 (his Messages 427 and 428; D-SQ-280): three letter rules, one per item, stated in each item's letter_rule. RANK within the population of stocks scored on the same scale (A top 10%; B next 15%, B+ its top half; C next 25% in thirds C+, C, C-; D next 25%; F bottom 25%) for the judgement items. His FIXED CUT-OFFS on the number (A 90 and above; B+ 82.5 to 89; B 75 to 82.4; C+ 66.67 to 74; C 58.33 to 66.66; C- 50 to 58.32; D 25 to 49; F below 25) for the items where 50 means neither positive nor negative: topics 1 and 2, Thesis's Change Forces' Strength, the External change forces and Internal change forces group judgements and their questions. The Rater's letter from his cut-offs on the MEASURE for topics 6, 8, 11 and 12, the number placed inside the letter's band. Rank and the percentile stay on every cell for information.
rule.scales: v1.5: every cell carries scale_tag; a rank letter is cut only among cells of the same scale (rater-v3 = the Rater v3.0 after the memo; rater-v2 and rater-v1-keyed = earlier Raters; writer-1.9 = the Investment Analyst's own score as it wrote the answer, the old method; writer-memo = the memo Analyst's own topic score). Old-method cells are labelled and stay until the Rater scores that stock's memo.
rule.scale_caveat: scores tagged rater-v1-keyed were set by the Rater of 1-Nov-26, whose key put 50 at the typical listed European company but was anchored on effect size rather than on percentiles; scores tagged rater-v2 or rater-v3 are standings in the Universe.

M:topic:1.note: set by the Rater; the Investment Analyst's own score was 78
M:topic:1.letter_rule: rank within this item's population of the same scale (A top 10%, B next 15%, C, D and F quarters; B+, B, C+, C, C- sub-grades)
M:topic:1.reason: Three operators' 4G capex (Airtel's cash capex tripled year on year, the top four African operators raised capex guidance by about a third) on top of a structural data and coverage gap gives broad, visible demand that lifts revenue about 10-11% for two years, but part of it is front-loaded from 2027-28 and customer-aligned tower ventures (Esengo, Indus, MTN-IHS) cap long-run pricing; consensus sales growth at the 70th percentile is honest for two years and then slows to 5-7%. A clear net positive, below Spie's mixed but structural grid pull and above Odfjell's two-year dayrate support, coherent with the group's 63.

M:topic:2.scale_version: the Rater v3.0, 2026-11-03: standing in the Universe of about 1,300 listed European companies (90 = better than about 9 in 10), every item scored after the memo is written, the case first on judgement topics, anchors from the corrected ordering of 75 companies, the question groups' keys (D-SQ-280)
M:topic:2.note: set by the Rater; the Investment Analyst's own score was 72
M:topic:2.letter_rule: rank within this item's population of the same scale (A top 10%, B next 15%, C, D and F quarters; B+, B, C+, C, C- sub-grades)
M:topic:2.reason: A funded, well-executed pivot from acquisitions to organic lease-up and distributions (buyback raised to 175 USDm, about 6% of market value, an inaugural growing dividend, refinancing cutting the cost of debt and three rating upgrades, ROIC from 10% to 14%) adds a few points a year to EPS through the share count and finance line, but it is narrow (no perimeter, pricing or cost-structure change) and dented by a cluster of governance and earnings-quality negatives. Below Redcare's larger operating-leverage pivot and above Teqnion's restructuring recovery, in line with the group's 62.

M:topic:3.scale_version: the Rater v3.0, 2026-11-03: standing in the Universe of about 1,300 listed European companies (90 = better than about 9 in 10), every item scored after the memo is written, the case first on judgement topics, anchors from the corrected ordering of 75 companies, the question groups' keys (D-SQ-280)
M:topic:3.note: set by the Rater; the Investment Analyst's own score was 71
M:topic:3.letter_rule: rank within this item's population of the same scale (A top 10%, B next 15%, C, D and F quarters; B+, B, C+, C, C- sub-grades)
M:topic:3.reason: A number-one independent position in seven of nine markets with 10-15 year non-cancellable indexed contracts, a 1% churn cap, 99.99% uptime and a density loop is a strong but defensive moat with no real pricing power, 72% customer concentration facing DRC renewals and frontier sovereigns; the 90th-percentile EBITDA margin and 82nd-percentile leverage reading show the profile, while 2% reported ROIC (17th percentile) understates incremental returns of about 20% pre-tax on new builds but the post-tax group return is only about at the cost of capital. I place it just below Tele2's rational oligopoly with cleaner returns and above Carlsberg, weighing the four groups (74, 68, 46, 66) with the weak economic strength pulling it below the qualitative parts.

M:topic:5.reason: About 215 USDm of the 420 USDm cash cost base is genuinely fixed and the rest is power passed through at nil margin, giving an 80% incremental EBITDA margin on a colocation; a fixed 180 USDm finance charge and a dollar tax charge then multiply each revenue dollar about three times on the way to EPS, with a reinforcing density loop. M:topic:2.reason: A complete sixteen-month reset delivered on time at good prices (new CEO, CFO and business-area heads; 15% of sales sold at 6.7x; SEK 500m impairment; preference shares redeemed; bonds refinanced from +4.90% to +2.00%; return on capital in pay; acquisitions restarted at about 6x with SEK 75m run-rate bought), already visible in return on capital (12.0% to 13.6%) and FY2027 estimates (+7% in three months); drop-through, 62% Q3 cash conversion, leverage at 2.9x and unattributed earn-out write-backs are still to be proved. Following Richard's ruling that the earlier 74 was too low, I weigh it above the Internal group's 69 because a change of this breadth that is already reaching estimates sits alongside NKT's working self-funded change, below Volex's raised targets and decade of self-made margin.

M:topic:4.letter_rule: rank within this item's population of the same scale (A top 10%, B next 15%, C, D and F quarters; B+, B, C+, C, C- sub-grades)
M:topic:4.reason: Near-term building blocks are conservative and being met (organic EBITA +4% to +6% against a 5% to 10% band, conversion 81% on twelve months), but over two to three years the company missed consensus in five of six quarters in 2024 to mid-2025, missed its organic EBITA targets in FY2024 and FY2025, saw FY2025 consensus EPS cut 44.5%, halved its 2025 acquisition target, has never raised a target, has missed margin four quarters running, and the SEK 100m 2026 deal target is more likely than not to be missed. Per Richard's ruling that 47 was too sanguine given the last two to three years, I place it below the Guidance group's 55: like Instalco a recent beat against a documented record of missed targets, slightly worse for the never-raised record, but above Hexatronic's five quarters of decline and walk-backs.

M:topic:5.scale_version: the Rater v3.0, 2026-11-03: standing in the Universe of about 1,300 listed European companies (90 = better than about 9 in 10), every item scored after the memo is written, the case first on judgement topics, anchors from the corrected ordering of 75 companies, the question groups' keys (D-SQ-280)

M:topic:5.letter_rule: rank within this item's population of the same scale (A top 10%, B next 15%, C, D and F quarters; B+, B, C+, C, C- sub-grades)
M:topic:5.reason: The structure gears through the balance sheet, not the income statement: a reinforcing loop (free cash flow buying SEK 90m to 100m of EBITA a year at 6.5x, which adds debt capacity) and a roughly fixed SEK 260m to 280m finance line falling from 27% to 14% of EBITA give EPS growth about 1.4 times revenue growth (16.3% against 11.5%, below the median company's 2x), while operating leverage is low (realised drop-through 20% to 25%, about the average margin, as units staff to two-month order books), pricing is partial and lagged, and there is no cost-out scope beyond SEK 35m to 50m already in the path. One strong evidenced element (the acquisition and finance loop) against weak operating gearing puts it a little above the ordinary mix, coherent with Economic strength 50 and Financial forecasts 63.

Consensus sales growth at the 72nd percentile fits; I sit with the External change forces group (63), below Eckert & Ziegler's more immediate structural pull and just above Odfjell's cyclical support.

M:topic:2.letter_rule: rank within this item's population of the same scale (A top 10%, B next 15%, C, D and F quarters; B+, B, C+, C, C- sub-grades)
M:topic:2.reason: The three-division reorganisation (Power's margin lifted from 1.0% to 5.3% by exiting commodity work), the pivot to programmes and own brand, the US expansion, a defence-industry chair and capacity built ahead are coherent and paid for, but on their own they move little earnings: overhead rose GBP 8.7m, the 12% group margin target was withdrawn, there is no capital-allocation step and the CEO succession was forced; the -3.0 point three-year margin change (25th percentile) reflects the cost built ahead. M:topic:3.reason: About 60% of revenue sits in accredited, designed-in defence and medical niches with a narrow real moat, but 39% is moat-less franchised distribution at a 4% margin, pricing power is only cost recovery, the radio business depends on a sole-source partner with undisclosed terms and one customer is 17% of revenue; management is honest and conservative but a passive allocator. M:topic:2.scale_version: the Rater v3.0, 2026-11-03: standing in the Universe of about 1,300 listed European companies (90 = better than about 9 in 10), every item scored after the memo is written, the case first on judgement topics, anchors from the corrected ordering of 75 companies, the question groups' keys (D-SQ-280)

M:topic:2.reason: The company's own actions are real and partly banked: leverage cut from 4.35x to about 2.3-2.5x, refinancing that drops net financial items from SEK 1,044m to a SEK 630m run-rate (most of 2026's 19% EPS rise), twenty loss-making units sold, SEK 738m of minority puts settled, and a 7x-disciplined deal restart of seventeen businesses, against a Services leadership vacuum (three heads in a year, the M&A head interim), no internal audit across 114 units and targets never met; the 3-year operating-margin change at the 52nd percentile confirms the operating change has not yet begun. M:topic:3.scale_version: the Rater v3.0, 2026-11-03: standing in the Universe of about 1,300 listed European companies (90 = better than about 9 in 10), every item scored after the memo is written, the case first on judgement topics, anchors from the corrected ordering of 75 companies, the question groups' keys (D-SQ-280)

M:topic:3.reason: Qualitatively a mediocre business made safe: an attractive, unconcentrated acquisition market but a weak position in it (higher cost of debt and equity, a two-to-three-turn compounding spread against twelve to fifteen at the leaders), no group moat, price-taker in construction, cost pass-through rather than pricing power, and a repair-proven management that has missed every target and lacks internal audit; ROIC 3.5% (26th percentile) and a 6.2% operating margin (23rd) are depressed by SEK 18bn of goodwill, but even new capital at 6.5-7x EBITA earns only modestly above its cost, while capital-light units and 163% FCF conversion (82nd) are genuine strengths. Coherent with the four groups (44, 28, 35, 40), it sits just below Zegona's owner-operator turnaround and above Instalco's lower-margin, barrier-free installation model, and below Teqnion (39) whose aligned CEO and margin records Storskogen lacks.

M:topic:1.letter_rule: rank within this item's population of the same scale (A top 10%, B next 15%, C, D and F quarters; B+, B, C+, C, C- sub-grades)
M:topic:1.reason: Judged on the continuing Automation perimeter: Vision has a real but partly refill-driven upturn (book up to EUR 170m, Jenoptik, Basler and Cognex strong, PMI 52.9) against Chinese 2D price pressure, while Machinery faces a tyre-maker capex freeze (book down 38%) that is a deferral with a replacement wave building; the strong grid and offshore tailwinds behind H1's 14% organic growth sit in Electrification, which is being sold, so they support the price, not the shareholder's future earnings. Net mildly positive over two to three years, a touch below the group's 60 because I weigh the Machinery trough as the force that sets FY2028, between OEM International's modest recovery and Kerry's neutral backdrop.

M:topic:2.letter_rule: rank within this item's population of the same scale (A top 10%, B next 15%, C, D and F quarters; B+, B, C+, C, C- sub-grades)
M:topic:2.reason: The most complete reset in TKH's history, largely on time: shareholder-approved separation of the worse 40% targeted for signing by Q1 2027, proceeds of about EUR 950m (nearly half the market value) turning 1.8x leverage into net cash with a buyback authorised, nine vision brands cut to two, capex programme finished, Eemshaven repaired and an external CEO from January; net of the internal problems that bear on it (unproven CEO, stranded costs arriving before savings, a thin capital-allocation record, working capital at 18.3% and 51.6% capitalised R&D). M:topic:1.reason: Defence, nearshoring, an electronics restocking pulse and EV and Medical recovery support about 12.6% organic growth in FY2027 (3 points of it copper, at no profit) and 5.5% to 6% after. M:topic:5.reason: This scores structure, and the structure has little gearing. Materials pass through and labour scales with volume (staff costs 23.1% of revenue in FY2020 and 22.6% in FY2026). Incremental margins of 10% to 14% sit close to the 10% average margin, real pricing power is absent and cost-out nets to 10bp to 20bp. EPS outgrows revenue (about 1.5 times, below the median company's 2 times) mainly because flat interest, a lower tax rate and a flat share count stop the leakage, which is light financial gearing rather than a reinforcing loop. So below the ordinary mix, and below the 56 to 62 of the groups, which reflect the financial strength and forecasts rather than the gearing.

Against them, the largest lung customer (Lung Bioengineering) is moving to its own platform, a step-down of 40-100 on a lung line of about 580 and the widest operating uncertainty of 2027; abdominal real price falls 1-2% a year against cheaper rivals; and the krona is a headwind. In line with Richard's ruling that 80 was far too high given the LBE customer risk, I place it at mild net positive, just above OEM International's recovering demand and below Odfjell's supportive cycle (groups: 60).
